h1: Baanbudsarin Apartment — Balcony Rooms at a Genuinely Low Price in Central Sing Buri
intro: If you want the cheapest stay in central Sing Buri with a bit of private space for an overnight stop or a few budget nights — Baanbudsarin Apartment is a name budget travelers and backpackers bring up often for its value. It's a 3-star apartment/hotel in the Bang Man area, opened around 2011, with many rooms available both daily and monthly, many of them with a balcony, plus a garden, a 24-hour front desk, free parking, and free Wi-Fi. What guests consistently praise is the very low price, the balcony rooms you can sit out on, and the central location with food close by. The trade-offs to know first: it's an older building, some rooms and bathrooms look worn with age, cleaning and upkeep can be inconsistent, and there's no breakfast or pool. Rooms start at approximately ฿400/night. From real guest reviews, couples score it around 8.1.

body.html: Baanbudsarin Apartment, known locally as Baan Budsarin, is a 3-star budget apartment/hotel at 190/39 Moo 7, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri. It has been open since around 2011 and offers many rooms on both daily and monthly terms. What keeps it on the radar of budget travelers and backpackers is simple: it's the lowest-priced option among in-town stays, many rooms come with a balcony, and the central location makes finding food easy — a good fit for anyone who wants a cheap overnight stop with a bit of private space.

Rooms come with air conditioning, a TV, a refrigerator, and an en-suite bathroom with a shower. Many rooms have a balcony and a small seating area, which several guests say they appreciate at this price — somewhere to catch the breeze or hang laundry. Room sizes range from singles up to larger family rooms. Reviews agree the value is strong for what you get, and it suits travelers who prioritize saving money and aren't expecting anything fancy.
"Very cheap rooms, with a balcony, cold A/C, free parking, right in town with food easy to find and Lotus nearby — great value for an overnight stop or a few budget nights."

Overall it's an in-town, apartment-style stay with a small garden, a 24-hour front desk, coin-operated laundry, a little on-site shop, and a massage service. But the honest part that reviews mention directly: the building is older, some rooms and bathrooms look worn with use, and cleaning and upkeep aren't always consistent. Some guests have run into bathroom problems and poor housekeeping, while many others report clean, fine rooms for the price. Your experience depends a lot on the room you get and the timing — so it's worth checking the latest room photos and recent reviews before booking. There's also no breakfast and no pool, and the front desk can be slow to respond at times.

The Bang Man location is convenient for self-drivers and anyone who wants to stay in town. It's about 1.5 km from Tesco Lotus, with a Thai à la carte restaurant near the property — a short walk or drive to food and shops. Wat Amphawan and Wat Phra Non Chakkrasi Worawihan are around 5 km away, and the Bang Rachan Heroes Monument and Bang Rachan Camp Park about 9 km — making it a workable budget base for exploring Sing Buri. It scores around 8.1 for couples across booking platforms, with price and location the most-praised points, while its Tripadvisor rating sits near 3.5 out of 5 — a sign that experiences here are genuinely mixed.

Honestly, Baanbudsarin Apartment is a budget stay for travelers focused on saving money while keeping a little private space — not a polished new hotel or a resort with a pool and breakfast. If you want newer rooms and more consistent upkeep on a modest budget, Central Park Hotel or Sing Buri Homestay may suit you better, and for a riverside feel try Chaisaeng Palace Hotel. But if your goal is the lowest price, a balcony room, and a central location with food close by, this place does the job for the money — just check the latest room photos and don't expect newness or breakfast.

Tips from following the reviews here: check the latest room photos and reviews before booking, and ask for a more recently renovated room or a better-kept floor, since room condition varies. Request a room with a balcony for the extra sitting and drying space. There's no breakfast, but you're near Lotus and town restaurants, so an early drive out for noodles or rice-and-curry is easy. Make the most of the free parking and low price — it's a short drive to Wat Phra Non Chakkrasi and the Bang Rachan sites. Compare Agoda and Booking each time, as prices shift around holidays, and note that at some periods the property asks for advance bank transfer to confirm — read the terms carefully first.
